home.kicker: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
home.heading: Welcome to Masjid Adam
home.aboutHeading: A small masjid with an open door
home.about:
A neighbourhood masjid on Bloor Street, open for all five daily prayers and two Jumu’ah congregations, with Qur’an classes for children and adults.

Everyone is welcome. If it is your first visit, our visitor guide explains what to expect.

announcements.title: Maktab Qur’an classes — enrol your child
announcements.body:
Daily Qur’an and Islamic studies classes for boys and girls, 4:30 PM to 6:30 PM on weekdays. Correct makharij, proper pronunciation, Islamic etiquettes, short hadith and basic fiqh with experienced teachers.

To register, call Br. Munawar at (416) 771-7999.

announcements.title: Hifz class — memorise the Qur’an
announcements.body:
A structured Hifz programme for boys, 6:00 PM to 7:30 PM on weekdays: makharij, sifat, memorisation techniques, revision and personalised support.

Call (416) 771-7999 to enrol.

announcements.title: Weekly Tafseer-ul-Qur’an with Imam Abdul Wali
announcements.body: Join us every Sunday after Maghrib salah for tafseer of the Qur’an. Refreshments are served. All are welcome.

learn.intro: Whether you grew up in the masjid or have never stepped inside one, this page is for you. It explains what happens here, why the prayer times change every day, and how to make the most of your visit.

visitorGuide.title: Everyone is welcome
visitorGuide.text: You do not need to be Muslim to visit. Come at any prayer time, or contact us to arrange a visit outside prayer hours.

visitorGuide.title: Shoes off, phones silent
visitorGuide.text: Shoes are removed at the entrance and placed on the racks. Please keep phones on silent inside the prayer hall.

visitorGuide.title: Dress modestly
visitorGuide.text: Loose clothing that covers the arms and legs is appreciated. Sisters are welcome to bring a headscarf; a few are available at the masjid.

visitorGuide.title: During prayer
visitorGuide.text: If you arrive while prayer is in progress, please wait quietly at the back until it finishes. You are welcome to sit and observe.

visitorGuide.title: Brothers and sisters
visitorGuide.text: There are separate prayer areas for brothers and sisters. Ask anyone at the door and they will point you the right way.

sections.title: Adhan and Iqamah
sections.body:
The **adhan** is the call to prayer. It marks the moment a prayer’s time begins, and it is calculated from the position of the sun — which is why the times shift by a minute or two every day.

The **iqamah** (also called *jama‘ah* time) is when the congregation actually lines up to pray together. The masjid fixes these times so that people can plan their day; they are usually rounded to a convenient time a little after the adhan and are updated every week or two as the seasons change.

On our prayer page you will see both: the adhan time (when the prayer comes in) and the iqamah time (when we pray together).

sections.title: How to perform wudu
sections.body:
Wudu is the washing done before prayer. Begin with the intention to purify yourself, then:

1. Say *Bismillah* and wash both hands up to the wrists three times.
2. Rinse the mouth three times.
3. Clean the nose by sniffing water in and blowing it out, three times.
4. Wash the whole face three times, from the hairline to the chin and ear to ear.
5. Wash the right arm up to and including the elbow three times, then the left.
6. Wipe the head once with wet hands, then wipe the ears.
7. Wash the right foot up to and including the ankle three times, then the left.

Wudu is broken by using the toilet, passing wind, deep sleep and a few other things — after which it is simply repeated. Washing facilities are available at the masjid.

sections.title: Friday prayer at Masjid Adam
sections.body:
Jumu’ah replaces the Dhuhr prayer on Fridays. It begins with a **khutbah** (sermon) in two parts, followed by a short two-rak‘ah prayer led by the imam.

Because our hall is small we hold **two Jumu’ah prayers**, at 2:00 PM and 3:30 PM, so that everyone has a chance to attend. Please arrive before the khutbah begins, listen quietly, and park only in the designated area — we share the street with our neighbours.

sections.title: Ramadan, Eid and the Islamic year
sections.body:
The Islamic (Hijri) calendar follows the moon, so each year is about eleven days shorter than the solar year and Islamic dates move earlier through the seasons.

**Ramadan** is the ninth month, when Muslims fast from dawn (Fajr) to sunset (Maghrib). The masjid provides **iftar** — the sunset meal — every evening for anyone who wishes to break their fast with us, and holds **Taraweeh**, the special night prayers of Ramadan, after Isha.

Ramadan ends with **Eid al-Fitr**; about ten weeks later, at the time of the Hajj pilgrimage, comes **Eid al-Adha**. Eid prayers are held at the masjid in the morning and are announced beforehand. Islamic dates on this site are approximate and are confirmed by the sighting of the new moon.

sections.title: Zakat and sadaqah
sections.body:
**Zakat** is the obligatory annual charity — 2.5% of savings held for a year above a minimum threshold — and is one of the five pillars of Islam. **Sadaqah** is any voluntary charity, given at any time and in any amount.

A **sadaqah jariyah** is a “continuing charity”: a gift whose benefit carries on, such as supporting a masjid or education. The Prophet ﷺ taught that when a person dies their deeds end except three — a continuing charity, beneficial knowledge, and a righteous child who prays for them. Supporting the masjid is one way to leave something that continues.
